case.lead: Technical case study — from data modeling to production deploy, the engineering decisions behind a clinical management platform.
case.problem.head: Running a clinic without a purpose-built platform
case.problem.p1: escuta… started as an internal tool for a psychoanalyst's practice and grew into a B2B clinical management SaaS — scheduling, clinical records/intake and finances in one place.
case.problem.p2: Before: scheduling in spreadsheets, fragmented records and manual finances, with no single source of truth. An off-the-shelf tool wasn't enough: clinical data demands confidentiality, and a practice demands fast, reliable answers.
case.arch.intro: A fullstack architecture designed for predictable performance and clinical-data confidentiality, from the system boundary down to the data layer.
case.arch.go.title: Zero-dependency backend in Go
case.arch.go.desc: A Go backend built on a zero-dependency philosophy: raw SQL (no ORM) and plain HTTP, in layers (cmd, models, repository, services, middlewares, handlers). Stripe over raw REST (no SDK) to keep go.mod clean and the binary small. Hosted on Render.
case.arch.db.title: Modeling & migrations in PostgreSQL
case.arch.db.desc: PostgreSQL on Supabase. Incremental, ADDITIVE .sql migrations (DEFAULT/NULL) so legacy data never breaks. A PARTIAL unique index on stripe_customer_id makes the webhook idempotent. Core tables: psicanalistas, pacientes, sessoes, pacotes.
case.arch.jwt.title: Access and trial enforced in the database
case.arch.jwt.desc: Stateless authentication via JWT. The 60-day trial is enforced in the database itself, with no credit card required — the subscription check lives in the API middleware, not in the front-end.
case.arch.infra.title: Split infra: Vercel + Render + Supabase
case.arch.infra.desc: Next.js on Vercel, the Go API on Render and PostgreSQL on Supabase. Stripe comes in over raw REST, and UptimeRobot keeps the free-tier service awake.
case.chal.avail.title: Availability on a free tier
case.chal.avail.problem: The API on Render (free tier) hibernated and Supabase dropped to 'degraded', causing timeouts and a blank screen on first visit.
case.chal.avail.solution: A static, ultra-light /health route (I removed the db.Ping) plus UptimeRobot keeping the service awake. On the front-end, request() with AbortController and a progressive timeout (20s on cold start, 12s afterwards), a single retry with backoff, fail-fast on 4xx/5xx and a "Waking the server up…" toast.
case.chal.billing.title: Billing without locking out the clinician (Fail-Open)
case.chal.billing.problem: How do you charge for a subscription without risking a clinical record being locked behind an infrastructure failure?
case.chal.billing.solution: A RequireActiveSubscription middleware built on a Fail-Open principle: if the Stripe check fails because of a database error, clinical access is granted. Gating is signalled with HTTP 402, intercepted globally on the front-end and redirected to /assinatura. The patient outranks the invoice.
case.chal.currency.title: Multi-currency without accounting errors
case.chal.currency.problem: Serving practitioners in BRL/USD/EUR/ARS without ever summing different currencies together.
case.chal.currency.solution: Visual multi-currency (no FX conversion); financial summaries use reduce to group by currency and format through Intl.NumberFormat.
case.diagram.title: Architecture flow
case.diagram.caption: The front-end on Vercel talks to the Go API on Render over REST/JSON; the API talks to PostgreSQL on Supabase over raw SQL, no ORM. Stripe sits at the edge as a webhook (REST integration, no SDK) and UptimeRobot hits /health to keep the free tier from hibernating.
case.schema.title: Core schema
case.schema.caption: Four tables carry the domain: psicanalistas, pacientes, pacotes and sessoes. The 60-day trial is a DEFAULT in the schema itself — a new account starts with a valid window, no card and no extra step in the application.
case.code.sql.title: Migration: partial unique index
case.code.sql.caption: The migration that makes the Stripe webhook idempotent. The index has to be PARTIAL because every trial account has no Stripe customer yet: a plain UNIQUE would allow only one row with a null stripe_customer_id.
case.code.go.title: Static /health handler
case.code.go.caption: The route that fixed hibernation. Dropping db.Ping decoupled the health check from Supabase — it answers as long as the process is serving HTTP, which is exactly what UptimeRobot needs to measure.
case.gallery.intro: Four product screens at full resolution, with technical notes on each flow.
case.shot.1.title: 01 · Dashboard
case.shot.1.cap: The practitioner's panel: active clients, sessions this week and month, no-show rate, session distribution by status and alerts for likely drop-off (patients with no session for over 30 days).
case.shot.2.title: 02 · Schedule
case.shot.2.cap: A weekly grid of one-hour slots: clicking a free slot opens booking, colours mark status (booked, confirmed, held, cancelled, no-show) and the footer closes out occupancy and pending confirmations.
case.shot.3.title: 03 · Community
case.shot.3.cap: A peer-supervision space for practitioners — clinical forum, case discussions and referrals — deliberately kept separate from the clinical record, which never leaves the patient's context.
case.shot.4.title: 04 · Landing & invite
case.shot.4.cap: The public product page during closed beta: value proposition, invite flow and the entry point to the practitioner login.
process.s1.d: I understand the problem, map requirements and define scope, success metrics and constraints.
process.s2.d: I model the domain and design the schema and service architecture before writing code.
process.s3.d: I build a type-safe back-end and front-end with modular, predictable code.
process.s4.d: I cover critical flows with tests and automate build, lint and tests in the pipeline.
process.s5.d: I ship with continuous deployment and monitor logs, metrics and alerts in production.
exp.e1.desc: A multi-tenant B2B SaaS for running clinical practices — scheduling, clinical records and billing. Front-end in Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind and Shadcn; back-end in Go (REST APIs) and PostgreSQL (Supabase with RLS). Shipped to production (Vercel/Render), handling database latency and compliance with the LGPD, Brazil's data protection law.
exp.e2.desc: Led the front-end of a complete education CRM and coordinated a team of 3 developers (code review, Git). React, Vite, Context API and CSS Modules. Authentication with access levels, student and enrolment management, and PDF certificate and report generation.
exp.e3.desc: High-conversion landing pages and React e-commerce sites (cart, checkout, payment integration), focused on performance and responsive design. React, JavaScript, Styled Components and Sass.

faq.q1: What role are you looking for?
faq.a1: A full-time remote position, junior to mid-level, in the React/Next + Go ecosystem. Brazil-first, open to international opportunities.
faq.q2: Which stacks do you work with?
faq.a2: Front: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind. Back: Go and Node with PostgreSQL. Infra: Vercel, Render, Supabase, Stripe.
faq.a3: By milestones, in vertical slices, validating before every commit (build + lint + typecheck), with Conventional Commits and living documentation in the repo.
faq.q4: Do you work end to end?
faq.a4: Yes — from data modeling and the API through to the front-end and deploy. escuta… is the proof: built solo, from the schema to Stripe.
